criteria.reasoning: The memo finds that "Director Aldana has an indirect ownership interest, through a Family Member (his wife Celeste, a spouse under Article II, Section 3)," and that Celeste M. Aldana is "the 100% owner." It concludes "Saffron & Sage was a conflict of interest that was not disclosed or addressed in the manner the policy requires."

The memo names both failures. First: "Aldana signed his 2026 statement on January 20, 2026 and answered 'No' to Question 2," while the bid "was received on January 8, 2026." Second, it records no pre-meeting notice and no oral disclosure, quoting the minutes: "No other director made a disclosure."

Under "No recusal (Article III, Section 3(a))," the memo states "Aldana did not leave the room during the discussion of the catering bid; on the contrary, he moved the motion to award the contract to Saffron & Sage and voted in favor of it." That covers the requirement to leave, his moving the motion and his vote.

The memo states only that "The motion carried 6-5." It never says that without Aldana's vote the result would have been 5-5, or that a tie would have failed. It does not address whether his vote decided the outcome.

The memo states "Harborview Provisions bid $52,900, Tidewater $55,750, and Saffron & Sage $68,400, a $15,500 spread," and that the Gala Committee "had, on January 29, recommended Harborview on price and prior performance." Both bids and the difference are correct.

The memo details Ramaswamy's annual-statement disclosure, her February 2 email to the Chair, her oral disclosure and her leaving the room, and records a "10-0 in favor; Ramaswamy absent" vote on the lowest $18,250 bid. It finds "the policy was followed. No further action is required under Article IV with respect to this transaction."

The memo identifies the reportable year as "the 2025 Form 990" for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2026, notes Saffron & Sage "is more than 35% owned by a family member of a director," and concludes "$71,860 paid. Below $100,000 (a) but above $39,400 (b). Reportable on Schedule L Part IV."
The memo states "1% of revenue is $39,400, and the threshold (b) figure is the greater of $10,000 or $39,400 = $39,400," based on total revenue of $3,940,000.

The memo treats BrightStage as an interested person (80% owned by a director's family member) and concludes "$18,250 paid. Below the $100,000 threshold (a) and below the $39,400 threshold (b). Not reportable."

Section 4a says "The committee must inform Director Aldana in writing of the basis for the committee's reasonable cause to believe he failed to disclose ... and give him 15 days to explain." Findings come only "After hearing Director Aldana's response." The memo calls the matter a "possible failure to disclose" and does not assert deliberate concealment or a decided sanction.

Section 4d says "the disinterested directors must re-review the transaction under Article III, Sections 3(c) and 3(d)," listing the $52,900 and $55,750 bids. It adds that if the Theatre paid more than fair market value, the board "shall consult legal counsel on whether the payment may be an excess benefit transaction under Internal Revenue Code section 4958 and on recovering the excess." It does not declare an excess benefit settled.

Section 4b says "Director Aldana must take no part in the Governance Committee's deliberations or votes on this matter, 'including as a member of the Governance Committee.'" The memo also recommends convening September 3 without him present for the Article IV items.

Section 4c says "The board, acting by a majority of the disinterested directors, determines whether he failed to disclose," then takes disciplinary and corrective action. Section 4e says he "shall file a corrected annual statement (Article VI) within 30 days of the board's determination."
